sections.body:
A plant is a living thing that makes its own food. You and I eat food. Plants build theirs from sunlight.

Every plant has the same main parts. The **roots** hold it in the soil and drink up water and minerals. The **stem** holds the plant up and carries water up from the roots. The **leaves** catch the sunlight. Flowers make seeds for the next plant. Fruit holds the seeds.

All of these parts are made of cells. A cell is one of the tiny building blocks that everything living is made of. Plants make new cells all the time, and that is what growing means.

Plants grow in two ways at once. They get taller, and they get wider. A tree gets taller at its tips and thicker at its base.

Here is the honest secret about plants: they do not hurry. A bean seed can sit in a drawer for a year and still grow when it finds water and warmth. The building is already packed inside the seed. All the seed needs is a wake-up call.
examples: Plants make their own food from sunlight.
The roots hold the plant and drink up water.
The seed was waiting for water and warmth to wake up.
sections.heading: What a plant is made of

sections.body:
A seed is a tiny packed-up plant with its own packed-up lunch. Under the hard coat there is a small root, a small shoot, and enough food for a few days.

Give the seed three things and it starts. It needs **water**, it needs **warmth**, and it needs **air**. It does not need light until the shoot comes up above the soil.

First the seed swells and its coat cracks. Then the root comes out first. Roots always go down, because they are looking for water and because they hold the plant in place.

The shoot comes out next. It pushes up through the soil and does not know which way is up. It feels the pull of gravity and turns to grow against it.

When the shoot reaches the light, the tip stops growing for a moment. Then the first leaves open. Those leaves start making food for the whole plant.

After that, the plant grows every day, in whatever direction has light, water and room.
examples: The seed coat cracked and the root came out first.
The shoot pushed up and turned towards the light.
The first leaves opened and started making food.
sections.heading: How a seed becomes a plant

sections.body:
You can watch a whole plant being built in about two weeks. You need a few beans, some cotton wool, a jar and a window.

Put the beans on damp cotton wool in the jar. Stand the jar somewhere warm. Then look at it every day and write down what you see.

Keep the cotton wool damp, not swimming. If you are not sure, touch it with a finger first.
examples: Day three: the seed is bigger and the coat has cracked.
Day five: a root is growing down and a shoot is pushing up.
Day ten: the leaves are open and green.
sections.heading: How to grow a bean and watch every part
steps: Soak a few beans in water overnight.
Put them on damp cotton wool in a clear jar.
Keep the jar in a warm spot, but not in hot sun.
Check every day and write down the changes.
Move the jar to a bright window when the shoots appear.

sections.body: Light, water, air and a little warmth are enough for most plants. Light lets the leaves make food. Water carries food up the stem and keeps the plant firm. Air is needed for the roots to breathe. Without light the plant grows pale and thin, because it cannot make food. Without water the leaves droop and the plant stops growing. Too much water drowns the roots, because they need air too. A plant in a pot also runs out of food, so it needs fresh soil now and then.
sections.heading: What plants need, and what happens without it

sections.body:
These are the words you need when you look closely at a plant.

Roots are the underground part. They anchor the plant and drink water and minerals from the soil.

The **stem** holds the plant up. It carries water up from the roots and food down to the roots.

Leaves are the food factories. Their green colour comes from chlorophyll, the stuff that catches sunlight.

Photosynthesis is the making of food. The leaf takes water from the stem, carbon dioxide from the air, and light from the Sun, and it makes sugar. The plant uses the sugar and gives out oxygen for us to breathe.
examples: The roots drink the water up from the soil.
The stem carries the water up to the leaves.
Photosynthesis is the making of food in the leaf.
sections.heading: The parts of a plant and their jobs

terms.example: The roots reached the water at the bottom of the pot.
terms.gloss: The part under the soil. It holds the plant in place and drinks up water and minerals.

terms.example: The stem was thicker this year than last year.
terms.gloss: The stalk of the plant. It holds the leaves up and carries water and food.

terms.example: The leaves turned yellow because the plant was in the dark.
terms.gloss: The green parts that catch sunlight and make food for the plant.

terms.example: Photosynthesis is why leaves are green and why we can breathe.
terms.gloss: The way a leaf makes sugar from light, water and air, and gives out oxygen.

sections.body:
Here is the part that surprises people most. A plant does not take food from the soil. It builds food for itself.

Inside the leaves there is a green substance called chlorophyll. It catches sunlight, and it uses that light to do a quiet piece of chemistry.

The leaf takes three things in. Water arrives from the roots and travels up the stem. Carbon dioxide, which is a gas in the air, comes in through tiny holes in the leaf. Light arrives from the Sun.

The leaf mixes them together and makes sugar. The plant uses the sugar to build more leaves, more stem, and more roots. It also stores some in the seeds, so the next plant has a packed lunch too.

What is left over goes out into the air as oxygen. That is the gas you breathe out and the plant breathes in. Plants and people share the air in a big, quiet partnership.

This is also why light matters so much. A plant kept in a dark cupboard keeps growing for a while, using its stored sugar. Then it runs out, and it grows thin, pale and weak.
examples: The leaf takes in water, air and light, and makes sugar.
The plant gives out the oxygen that we breathe.
In the dark the plant ran out of sugar and went pale.
sections.heading: How a plant makes its own food

item.summary: Every plant starts small and builds itself one part at a time. A seed wakes up, sends down a root, pushes up a shoot, opens leaves and makes its own food from light, water and air. After reading this you can grow a seed and watch each part appear, name the parts of a plant, and explain how a plant makes its food.
item.title: How Do Plants Grow?
